gaps.sentence: The manuscript is too fragile ___ (handle) without gloves.
gaps.explanation: Passive to-infinitive: to be + past participle. The manuscript receives the handling.

gaps.sentence: The ambush ___ (plan) by someone with intimate knowledge of the valley.
gaps.explanation: Past perfect passive (had been planned) stresses completion before the ambush; was planned is also acceptable.

gaps.sentence: The whole street ___ when the gas main burst.
gaps.explanation: The street was evacuated by others: past necessity had to be + evacuated.

gaps.sentence: I need this report ___ by noon, not five.
gaps.explanation: Need + object + past participle: the report is typed by somebody else (causative-like).

gaps.sentence: Nothing ___ about the incident until the inquiry began.
gaps.explanation: Nothing was known by anybody: past simple passive was + known.

gaps.sentence: He's getting his eyes ___ next week.
gaps.explanation: Causative get + object + past participle: getting his eyes tested (by an optician).

gaps.sentence: The decision ___ (announce) at yesterday's press conference.
gaps.explanation: 'Yesterday' signals past simple passive: was + announced.

gaps.sentence: The matter ___ at this very moment, so no comment yet.
gaps.explanation: Look into (investigate) passivises with the particle kept: is being looked into.
